verdict_reason: The erank kernel is verbatim Roy & Vetterli 2007 Def. 1 / Eq. (1) (p_k = sigma_k/||sigma||_1, erank = exp H(p) on RAW singular values). Feeding the paper's own Sec. 2.3 4x4 correlated matrix through numpy SVD and BLME's effective_rank reproduces the published closed form exp{2H((1+|rho|)/2,(1-|rho|)/2)} at rho = 0/0.25/0.5/0.75/0.9 with worst relative error 2.99e-16 (rho = 0.5: 3.079201435678004 against 3.079201435678004), and Property 1 (k equal singular values -> k) holds to 5.68e-16 for k = 1,2,3,5,10,50. Both CODE defects that held this task at YELLOW from BOTH reviewers in round 4 are FIXED at the state I reviewed: collapse.py:193 now computes min_erank/max_erank with NO +1e-12 (two identical rank-one layers return exactly 1.0 instead of 0.9999999999989999, abs err 1.000089e-12 removed), and utils.effective_rank:41-55 returns NaN, not 0.0, for a spectrum with no positive singular value -- restoring Property 1's 1 <= erank(A) range and routing a degenerate layer into the existing nanmin/nanmax/_meta_n_failed_layers accounting instead of silently driving collapse_ratio to 0.0. I constructed no value-changing counterexample on the paper-defined domain. ADJUDICATION: both round-4 reviewers returned YELLOW for the same reason -- the +1e-12 in collapse_ratio -- and both were right about the code AS IT STOOD. That epsilon is gone at this state (collapse.py:193), together with the effective_rank 0.0-on-degenerate return, so the shared objection no longer has an object.
comparable_reason: max_erank / min_erank / max_drop are raw DIMENSION COUNTS, not scale-free quantities. On a structureless iid Gaussian null at fixed N = 1200 the effective rank runs 7.9892 (d = 8) -> 31.8860 (32) -> 126.2017 (128) -> 480.5317 (512), i.e. a 60x move over a 64x width range with no change in the underlying geometry. They are additionally a function of the realized token population, which defaults.yaml does not pin -- num_samples: 100 counts DOCUMENTS, so two models with different tokenizers and document lengths are scored at different N. collapse_ratio itself is far better behaved because it is a ratio of two eranks measured in the SAME model at the SAME N, and the erank profile is exactly invariant under an isometry: zero-padding a fixed rank-8 cloud from d = 8 to d = 512 leaves erank at 7.992182755 and the participation ratio at 7.937838479, bit-identical.
github_reason: Fetched the released spectrum.py from facebookresearch/directclr (147 lines, HTTP 200). Its singular() L2-row-normalizes the latents, transposes, forms np.cov and returns np.linalg.svd's singular values -- grep for 'effective_rank' or 'exp(' returns 0 hits, so the release contains NO effective-rank, exponential-entropy or collapse-ratio routine and there is no matched scalar to run head to head; executing it at all needs an ImageNet val loader, a ResNet-50 checkpoint and CUDA. Roy & Vetterli 2007 (EUSIPCO), which is the actual source of the formula BLME computes, is a 2007 conference paper with no released code. Cross-verification was therefore done against that paper's own closed form and against an independent exp(-sum p log p) implementation (see paper_reason).
paper_reason: Roy & Vetterli 2007 Sec. 2.3 gives erank = exp{2 H((1+|rho|)/2, (1-|rho|)/2)} for their correlated 4x4 example. BLME's effective_rank on the actual matrix returns 4.000000000000000 / 3.755143410318479 / 3.079201435678004 / 2.124508162217515 / 1.487401275304271 against the closed form 4.000000000000000 / 3.755143410318479 / 3.079201435678004 / 2.124508162217516 / 1.487401275304271 at rho = 0 / 0.25 / 0.5 / 0.75 / 0.9 -- worst relative error 2.99e-16. Property 1 gives exactly k for k = 1,2,3,5,10,50 (worst rel 5.68e-16). collapse_ratio and max_drop are BLME extensions on top of that profile and have no published counterpart.
confounds_reason: The raw profile keys ARE effective-dimension counts and therefore track d_model directly: on a no-structure iid null the erank rises 7.9892 -> 480.5317 over d = 8 -> 512 (a 60x change from width alone) and the participation ratio 7.9165 -> 358.5887. They also track the realized point count. This is a property of the estimand, not a defect: the same sweep leaves the value bit-identical under an exact zero-padding isometry (7.992182755 at d = 8, 64 and 512), so what moves is genuine ambient dimension use, not an arithmetic artifact. collapse_ratio, being a within-model min/max, is the key that should carry a cross-model claim.
